evidence: src/infrastructure/composition/createRepositories.ts: `export interface Repositories { projects; tasks; users }` and `createRepositories()` are the only place where InMemoryProjectRepository, InMemoryTaskRepository and InMemoryUserRepository are created.

src/infrastructure/composition/taskModule.ts: `createTaskController(repositories: Repositories, ids: IdGenerator)` destructures `{ projects, tasks, users }` from Repositories and does not create repositories directly.
All three controller factories share the same signature and build pattern, so they use the abstraction consistently and keep each piece of wiring separate.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All four files deal with one concern: composing the dependency graph (the composition root). createRepositories.ts holds the one place where concrete in-memory repository implementations are chosen, and it exposes them through the Repositories interface. projectModule.ts, taskModule.ts and userModule.ts each wire one controller from application services. All three take the same (repositories: Repositories, ids: IdGenerator) parameters and get repositories only through the Repositories abstraction. None of them create persistence implementations directly, so none of them go around the module's own abstraction. No rule or invariant is repeated: repository construction happens only in createRepositories, and each controller factory wires a separate set of services. Import direction is out of scope for this review.
